note: Every output of the calculator is an estimate. Universities and credential-evaluation services apply their own rules, and the German formula below is described by the German universities that publish it as non-binding orientation only.
_scales: Nmax is the best achievable grade and Nmin the lowest passing grade; both feed the modified Bavarian formula. 'gpa' says how a 4.0 GPA is derived: 'bands' uses the letter bands below, 'direct' means the input already is a 4.0 GPA, 'letters' uses the letter map, and null means no published conversion exists, so the calculator shows no GPA for that scale.

gpa4.label: 4-point scale (GPA)
gpa4.note: On a 4.0 scale the lowest passing grade is a D, which is 1.0. Some German universities use 2.0 instead; the German figure shifts if yours does.

uz100.label: 100-point (university transcript)
uz100.caution: Scholaro puts the pass mark at 55. WES has described 51% as passing for Uzbek undergraduate study, and individual universities set their own mark, so check your own transcript.

percent.label: Percentage (%)
percent.note: Treated exactly like the 100-point transcript scale, which is how Uzbek universities report percentages.

ib.label: International Baccalaureate (Diploma total)
ib.note: 24 is the minimum total for the IB Diploma and 45 the maximum. There is no official IB-to-GPA conversion, so the calculator shows the German grade and your profile strength but no 4.0 GPA.

alevel.label: A-Level (average grade)
alevel.note: E is the lowest passing A-Level grade. There is no official A-Level-to-GPA conversion, so no 4.0 GPA is shown.

german.name: Modified Bavarian formula
german.disclaimer: German universities that publish this formula state that the result is non-binding and serves only as a first orientation.

uk.basis: These are the GPA ranges the University of Southampton publishes as equivalent to a UK degree classification. Other UK universities set slightly different ranges.
uk.note: A UK class is a degree classification, so it is only shown for university-level grades.

_profile: minRatio is the position on your own grading scale, (Nd − Nmin) ÷ (Nmax − Nmin), so it works for every scale including IB and A-Level.
_countries: `data` names the file in /data holding a comparable university list. Countries without one are offered in the form, but the shortlist says plainly that we do not have a comparison list for them yet rather than inventing universities.

tests.label: TOEFL iBT
tests.note: TOEFL iBT moved to a new 1–6 scale on 21 January 2026. Check which scale the university you are applying to is using.

tests.label: TestDaF / Goethe
tests.note: Goethe certificates report a CEFR level rather than a score; if you hold one, tell us the level in the consultation.

shortlist.note: The grouping below uses only the QS rank held in the country data files, each university's published selectivity and, where a university publishes a minimum English score, how your score compares with it. It is not a prediction of whether you will be admitted — nobody can give you that.

sources: TU Darmstadt — Notenumrechnung (modified Bavarian formula, KMK)
University of Southampton — Entry qualification equivalencies, United States
Duolingo English Test — Understand scoring (10–160, 5-point steps)
